title: ECB picks Spain's Hernández de Cos as president, with 3 tests waiting from day one
body: For bonds, the appointment matters most for the gap between French and German yields. Markets may treat a president who backed quantitative easing as a slightly firmer safety net for French debt, but his record on fiscal discipline makes a blanket rescue unlikely. That leaves French spreads tied to the election campaign more than to the ECB. The euro's immediate reaction is likely to be muted, since Hernández de Cos is seen as a continuity candidate, not someone who will change the direction of rates. Brunnermeier as chief economist is worth watching, as his academic work on financial stability could shape how the bank thinks about stepping into markets. --- Earlier heads up on this: EU leaders set to confirm backing for Spain's De Cos as next ECB President - report --- Europe has handed the ECB to a soft-spoken Spanish technocrat who backed quantitative easing but preaches fiscal discipline, and France's shaky bond market and looming election may test which instinct wins within weeks of his arrival.

title: JPMorgan sees bitcoin capitulation in record Strategy discount, but 3 risks cloud the call
body: For bitcoin, the June closing low near $58,500 is now the key level. A clean break would put the next on-chain support clusters, around $57,000 and then $47,000, in play, and would probably trigger more selling from miners whose costs sit well above the price. For Strategy shareholders, forced selling by index funds around the November 30 MSCI removal could widen the discount further before any rebound. Heavy options positioning could make moves in either direction more violent. A recovery in the ratio back above 1, as happened in July, would be the clearest sign that sellers are finished. --- Earlier: Bitcoin consolidates at yearly lows as traders await fresh catalyst amid negative backdrop --- JPMorgan reads Strategy's record discount to its bitcoin holdings as a sign that selling may be nearly exhausted, but ETF outflows, struggling miners and a looming index removal mean the market has yet to confirm a bottom.

title: NZX 50 Sets 2nd Straight Weekly Loss Ahead of Election Results
body: The NZX 50 slipped 30 points, or 0.2%, to 13,957 in Friday morning trading, extending the previous session's losses as investors remained cautious ahead of the final general election results due later today. Sentiment was further pressured by concerns over a proposed US move to impose new tariffs on 14 trading partners, stoking fears of potential interest rate hikes. Market participants also kept a close watch on the conflict in the Middle East and its effect on oil prices, given ongoing inflation risks. Attention was turning to the release of New Zealand's business confidence figures and China's PMI data, both scheduled for next week. Fresh data showing New Zealand's consumer confidence returning to positive territory helped limit further declines. Still, healthcare and communication services stocks weighed on the benchmark. Early notable decliners included Henderson Far East Income (-1.2%), Brisco Group (-1.0%), Fisher & Paykel (-0.7%), and Chorus (-0.5%). For the week, the NZX 50 lost 1.1%, marking its second consecutive weekly decline. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Mexican Peso Extends Longest Losing Streak in Five Years
body: The Mexican peso weakened to about 19.7 per USD, its lowest level since April 2025, extending its longest losing streak in five years as investors shifted into safe-haven assets and unwound popular carry trades. Mounting concerns around the AI-driven rally triggered a broad risk-off tone, boosting demand for safer assets such as the US dollar and putting additional pressure on Latin American currencies. Over the past three months, the peso has fallen more than 13%, following signals from Banxico that it was open to easing, and its subsequent quarter-point cut in the benchmark rate to 6.25% in early November. In the context of likely rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, this move has eroded the attractiveness of carry trades, which are also being undermined by strains in the AI trade and rising volatility that is chipping away at returns. Currency volatility is expected to remain high in the coming months amid ongoing uncertainty over the Fed's policy path and increasingly stretched valuations in AI-related assets. title: European Stocks Close Higher
body: European equities advanced on Thursday, mirroring the rebound in AI-related stocks in North America as markets reassessed the downside risks from potential cuts in AI spending. The Euro STOXX 50 climbed 2.2% to 6,025, while the STOXX Europe 600 added 1.9% to reach 638. Technology shares led the gains, suggesting that some investors view this week's selloff in AI stocks as excessive. The move highlighted both the uncertainty and the inherently speculative nature of expected returns from AI deployment. ASML and Infineon jumped 3.2% and 4%, respectively. Sentiment was further supported by indications that upcoming US tariffs may be less punitive than initially anticipated, with duties on EU imports now expected to be capped at around 15%. Banks also finished sharply higher, with Santander rising 4% and BNP Paribas up 3%. In the corporate sector, SAP gained 2.3% after announcing plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs, equivalent to roughly 9% of its global workforce.
